citation.title: Automatic analysis of JET charge exchange spectra using neural networks
citation.authors: C M Bishop, C M Roach, M G von Hellermann
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown; no DOI is printed in the supplied PDF

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1-10 (PDF p1 is the publisher cover; PDF p2-10 are journal pp 765-773)
scope_read.limitations: Scanned text with OCR errors. Figure axes are only partly legible. The paper does not tabulate per-parameter errors.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: A neural network gives an approximate, unsupervised reading of CX spectra.
claim_checks.source_finding: About 3000 JET BeIV/CIII spectra had been fitted by least squares. Several networks used subsets of the 600 spectral bins as inputs; the largest was 50-15-6. Ion temperature agreed with the conventional fits to about 30%. The results are labelled preliminary, and one spectrum is reconstructed with residuals of roughly ±0.15 of the conventional amplitude.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p7-8, Sec 4; PDF p8, Figs 4-5; PDF p9, Sec 4 end
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Neural networks have long been used to read CX spectra directly. For example, networks trained on least-squares-fitted JET spectra produced approximate line parameters without an initial guess (Bishop et al 1993).
claim_checks.qualification: The comparison is against conventional fit labels, not physical truth. It is a single-frame spectrum reading. The 30% figure is not comparable to our metrics.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The network output can initialise least-squares fitting.
claim_checks.source_finding: The authors propose a hybrid in which the network supplies the initial guess for the iterative fit, with fewer iterations expected. The hybrid is not implemented or evaluated.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p2, Abstract; PDF p9, Sec 5 para 2
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The authors proposed using such network estimates to initialise iterative fitting.
claim_checks.qualification: Describe this as a proposal, not a demonstrated hybrid.

claim_checks.source_finding: The paper measures 15 ms per spectrum for the unoptimised network versus a 500 ms average for the conventional fit, both on the JET IBM mainframe. That is about 33x, although the introduction states 'typically two orders'. Suitability for analogue or real-time hardware is asserted by analogy to COMPASS equilibrium-control hardware.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p9, Sec 4; PDF p3, Sec 1; PDF p2, Abstract; PDF p9, Sec 5 para 3
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: They reported faster offline processing than least-squares fitting and suggested hardware implementation for real-time use.
claim_checks.qualification: No CX real-time deployment is reported. Do not reuse the 'two orders' wording.

input_target_timing.inputs: Selected wavelength bins of the same CX spectrum (subsets of 600 bins); four networks covered parameter subsets
input_target_timing.outputs: Line amplitudes, positions and widths for that spectrum; ion temperature is derived from these
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Offline, same-frame inverse fitting; no temporal forecasting
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes: the CX spectrum itself is the input
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Targets are conventional least-squares results (PDF p6, Sec 3 step 1); no independent truth

validation.split_unit: Train/test splitting is described generically (PDF p6, Sec 3 step 2); the split used for the reported results is not stated
validation.unknowns: Test-set size, shot grouping, error distributions and uncertainty are not reported. A forward chi-squared check is proposed but not shown (PDF p10, Sec 5).

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Mainframe processing time per spectrum: 15 ms (network) vs 500 ms average (conventional)
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Real-time or in-loop CX operation, the hybrid fit's speed or accuracy, and hardware implementation for CX
runtime_or_deployment.locator: PDF p9, Sec 4 last para; PDF p9, Sec 5

forbidden_inferences: The paper performed causal or temporal nowcasting.
The method was deployed in real time.
The hybrid initial-guess scheme was demonstrated.
The source was the first neural network for CX spectra, or it establishes any priority.
The source supports KSTAR, BES/ECEI or pedestal claims.
Faster spectrum reading by itself benefits our nowcast.
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. This is an upstream reader of an available spectrum. Our method estimates the current CES report before it is available, using past reports plus BES/ECEI. Faster reading could refresh anchors or reduce the need for nowcasting; any benefit is untested.
